issues.claim: V05 §3.16 (4)'s landfall table has no rule for a covered part already further down its ladder than the row's outcome. The wall row keeps a run already breached or dismantled ('the ladder only stepping down'). The raised row (l. 1342) writes `ruined` and the retaining row (l. 1343) writes `decayed`, with no such rule. V06 §3.19.2 (4) says 'a landfall ruins the spans and supports it covers whatever their state'. So a `cleared` span or support (its stone salvaged, V06 §3.19.2 (3)) is written back to `ruined`, and a `ruined` retaining run (its stone gone) back to `decayed`. The results are wrong: a released way counts as standing again (V06 §3.19.1 (3): 'every span standing or ruined, none cleared') and is repaired by V06 §3.19.2 (5), though 'a dismantled span or a cleared support is never rebuilt'; its 'rubble' is salvaged again, so the ledger credits the same stone twice; the retaining run is repaired by `repairRetaining` though 'a ruined stretch ... is not restored'; and a `cleared` member has no op to end its cover, so the decoration never closes. T-V5-14's new round-6 passage (l. 2562–2565) runs a landfall over a span 'already ... `cleared`' and 'a support by the run's band `cleared`' and asserts only 'by theirs'. A literal build passes the wrong result, while a builder reading the wall row's ladder keeps `cleared`.
issues.required_change: V05 §3.16 (4), raised row: '`ruined` (item 244's span and support `state`);' -> '`ruined` (item 244's span and support `state`) — one already `ruined` kept, one already `cleared` (its stone taken, V06 §3.19.2 (3)) kept `cleared` and never a member, the state only stepping down as the wall row's ladder does;'. Retaining row: '`decayed` over its covered length (item 245's state,' -> '`decayed` over its covered length, a run of it already `ruined` (its stone gone) kept `ruined`, the state only stepping down (item 245's state,'. §3.16 (5): 'and the covered raised spans and raised-way piers, each by its raised way' -> 'and the covered raised spans and raised-way piers not `cleared`, each by its raised way'. §3.23's 'the landfall' row (l. 1774) adds the input 'a covered span or support already `cleared`; a covered retaining run already `ruined`' with the outcome 'kept as it is, no member' (T-V5-14). T-V5-14: 'a span over the run already `ruined` and, on a second run, `cleared`' -> '... `cleared` (kept `cleared`, no member, its way still released, V06 §3.19.1 (3))'; 'a support by the run's band `cleared`' -> '... `cleared` (kept `cleared`, no member)'. END V06 §3.19.2 (4): 'a landfall ruins the spans and supports it covers whatever their state' -> 'a landfall ruins the spans and supports it covers, standing or already `ruined`, a `cleared` one kept `cleared` (V05 §3.16 (4))'.

issues.claim: §2.7's crossing table, row W8's C2 cell (base l. 2705) re-lays an arch vault after `absorbWall` 'once the record is dropped'; T-V6-11 (V6-20, l. 4134) says the same. No op drops a cleared enceinte record. V06 §3.7.2 (3) keeps it in the fortification loop 'until every run is `dismantled`' and keeps it after that as what the `enceinte` provider reads (l. 1488–1499). The rule for the vault reads the band and strip, not the record: *beneath* reads a `vault` span `open` 'while that band or strip lies there, whatever the runs' condition', and V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1) lays the chamber 'once none does'. `absorbWall` merges the strips (band + setback + glacis) into the blocks (V06 §2.8, §3.7.2 (3)), so none lies there from its own commit. `EpochScope.raised` (V06 l. 465, W64) admits the raised way only for 'a wall the epoch laid, moved or removed', and never says whether an absorb counts. Builders therefore diverge: re-lay the vault at `absorbWall`, at the last run's dismantling, or never. T-V6-11's bar has no event to time it by.
issues.required_change: Model, §2.7's crossing table, row W8, C2 cell: 'V04 lays again an arch vault the wall stood over once the record is dropped' -> 'V04 lays again, in `absorbWall`'s commit, an arch vault the wall stood over (its strips and band merged into the blocks, none lies there any more; V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1))'. END V06: T-V6-11 'V04 laying again the arch vault of a `vault` span the old wall stood over once the record is dropped' -> 'V04 laying again, in `absorbWall`'s epoch, the arch vault of a `vault` span the old wall stood over (its strips and band merged, none lying there)'; §2.1's `EpochScope.raised` comment and W64 'a wall the epoch laid, moved or removed' -> 'a wall the epoch laid, moved, absorbed (`absorbWall`) or removed'; §2.8's `absorbWall` comment 'its strips re-join the blocks beside them' -> 'its strips, the band with them, re-join the blocks beside them (no band or wall strip lies on the old line after it, §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'. END V04: the epoch reconcile bullet (l. 2286) 'a wall the epoch laid, moved or removed' -> 'a wall the epoch laid, moved, absorbed or removed'.

issues.claim: Round-6 note (6) (b) (i) asks that each cell name a test that runs it; R5-10, kept by R6-11, says the same. §2.7's crossing table names V06's tests in cells whose raised-way state those tests never set up: row W5 (decay) C3–C8, C10, C12, C13 name T-V6-73, which runs only C2 (the aqueduct standing); row W6 (gate opening) C3–C8, C10, C12, C13 name T-V6-47, which runs no gate opening beside any other state; row W8 (`absorbWall`) C3–C6, C8, C10, C12, C13 name T-V6-11, which runs only C2. V05's repair ran row W12's cells in T-V5-14; V06's repair did not run its rows. The outcomes are defined (*unchanged meeting*), so nothing built changes.

T-V6-11, after its absorb clause, add '; the same absorb, each on its own run, with the aqueduct in each other state row W8 names this test for (a span over the ring fallen, every span fallen, a support by its band `cleared` and, on a second run, `ruined`, locked, a fallen span repaired by `repairRaised`, extended by a frame growth, re-spaced by a hand `spanSpacingCm` edit) — each an *unchanged meeting*'. T-V6-47 adds '; the CITY ring's pathway opening its gates (V06 §3.7.2 (1)) beside its standing aqueduct and, each on its own run, in each other state row W6 names this test for (a span over the ring fallen, every span fallen, a support by its band `cleared`, the aqueduct deleted, locked, repaired, extended by a frame growth, re-spaced) — no gate it opens under a deck'.

issues.claim: T-V6-47 (V6-21, l. 4170) takes T110-2 (7) with its own script: 'a `vault` span in the circuit's band breached and a support by the band dismantled by scripted `DeclineOp`s (as its lapse's salvage would, V06 §3.19.2 (3); E3's ops)'. A trace crosses an aqueduct only under a span (*beneath*), so the supports by the band bound the breached span, and only that span is breached. V06 §3.19.2 (3) dismantles only 'a support both of whose spans are ruined or cleared', and T-V6-61 holds '0 supports cleared while a span beside them stands' on H-AQUA. The script, as written, leaves a standing span on a cleared support; the base's (7) avoids this by making a span over the band `ruined` as well. The test also omits the later-laid order. Row W1·C5 (and W1·C3) names T-V6-47 for 'laid after the fall, through a `cleared` ring as open ground', which V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s new `cleared` clause governs. T-V6-47 runs only the order in which the circuit comes first; the base's (7) holds the other order ('in the cells' own order').
issues.required_change: In T-V6-47 replace 'a `vault` span in the circuit's band breached and a support by the band dismantled by scripted `DeclineOp`s (as its lapse's salvage would, V06 §3.19.2 (3); E3's ops)' with 'a `vault` span in the circuit's band breached, then the span beyond one of its supports breached and that support, both its spans fallen, dismantled, by scripted `DeclineOp`s (as its lapse's salvage would, V06 §3.19.2 (3); E3's ops)'. After 'the delete's undo restoring the cap' add '; and, in the cells' own order, an epoch circuit laid across the aqueduct after a span over its planned band fell `ruined` and after a support there was `cleared` — the run at its own top beneath the fallen span, the trace through the cleared ring as open ground (V06 §3.7.6 (5)) — and an epoch contraction laid after a support by its planned line was `cleared` — the trace through its former ring'.

issues.claim: Two round-6 clauses need a `vault` span at H-AQUA's crossings. T-V6-11 (V6-20) has 'V04 laying again the arch vault of a `vault` span the old wall stood over', which needs the span over the CITY ring's band. T-V6-47 (V6-21) has 'a `vault` span in the circuit's band breached', which needs the span the METROPOLIS circuit crosses under. The span rule draws `vault` by chance against `span.vaultShare[kind]` × `raisedVaultM` (base l. 2740). H-AQUA's definition (l. 4057–4071) holds neither span and the fixture list names neither case. This is the class R5-10 and R6-11 rule on: a fixture must hold its case.
issues.required_change: V06 §7's H-AQUA: after 'on a span over its band (§2.7's crossing table, *over the band*)' insert '— the recipe's seed searched so that this span, and the span under which the METROPOLIS epoch's circuit later crosses the aqueduct, each reads `vault` in its record (§2.7's span rule; read `open` while a wall lies under it, *beneath*) —'.

issues.claim: T-V6-73's new founded-viaduct clause (V6-22, l. 4196) and T110-2 (2) (base l. 18552) bar 'not founded, `raised.waited` at each epoch'. That cannot hold at every epoch of H-AQUA (TOWN → CITY → METROPOLIS → TOWN). At a TOWN epoch no founding is admitted (`raised.generatedBelowCity`, V06 §3.19.1 (4)), so nothing waits. Once the CITY ring's trace is gone by its pathway (`wallToWay`), the course no longer crosses a standing trace.
issues.required_change: T-V6-73: '`raised.waited` at each epoch' -> '`raised.waited` at each CITY and METROPOLIS epoch while the CITY ring's trace stands'. END scope: the same words in §13.2's T110-2 (2).
